subject: NimblePay internal sell-in kit & procurement timeline
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@nimblepay.com>
Cc: Tom Harris <tharris@nimblepay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + quick asks (next steps)

Hi Sara — thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap from our side and the asks to keep momentum:

Summary:
- Goal: pilot Redwood to reduce inference cost and latency for NimblePay’s fraud detection scoring (batch + realtime).
- Key success metrics (from call): reduce per-API latency to <120ms p95 for online scorer; 3x throughput improvement for batched jobs; 25% unit-cost reduction via batching/caching.
- Current pilot scope proposed: 6-week PoC, 2 models (scoring + reranker), staged rollout to 10% traffic.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the economic buyer and the procurement timeline? You mentioned Finance + Procurement sign-off — who should we loop?
2) Legal touchpoint: if you can share the name/email of the legal reviewer (or point to your general legal queue), we’ll prepare the contract with standard MSA + DPA.
3) Security questionnaire: we’ll send our SOC2 summary and a short evidence packet. Any specific compliance docs needed beyond SOC2 and network diagrams?
4) Internal enablement: we’ll assemble a one-pager and 3-minute demo script for your internal advocate(s). Who on your side will be championing this?

I’ve attached the draft PoC scope and a short one-pager for internal sharing. If possible, can you get back with buyer/legal/procurement names and a target decision week (e.g., week of Oct 4)?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the internal enablement pack once we have the names.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments:
- nimblepay_poc_scope.pdf (12 pages)
- nimblepay_internal_onepager.pdf (1 page)
From: Tom Harris <tharris@nimblepay.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@nimblepay.com>, Amy Chen <amy.chen@nimblepay.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quick asks (next steps)

Alex — appreciate the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Economic buyer: Sara Liu (Head of Payments Product) will own the business case, but final budget sign-off runs through Finance (Kristen Park, finance@nimblepay.com). Sara will be the champion for product ROI and internal buy-in.

2) Procurement: Procurement will run the contracting process — procurement@nimblepay.com. Typical cycle is ~2 weeks for standard SaaS MSAs; if there are exceptions it can take longer.

3) Legal: Amy Chen (copied) is our primary legal reviewer for third-party contracts. Amy — could you confirm if a redline is expected or if you prefer our standard attachment?

4) Security/compliance: SOC2 + network diagram is our baseline. If you have a short evidence pack (keys/controls, data handling summary) that’d be ideal. We do not require SaaS-hosted inventory at the PoC stage but will request architecture diagrams for Private deployment later.

Target timeline: Sara and I would like a decision calendarized for the week of Oct 4–8. That gives us time to align Finance and Procurement.

Also — Sara asked for an internal one-pager and a short talk track that she can use with the exec sponsor (CFO). If you can draft a 1-page business case and two 30-second soundbites we can use, that would be helpful.

Thanks,
Tom
Senior Product Manager, NimblePay
tharris@nimblepay.com
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap + quick asks (next steps) — prep for internal sell-in

Team — forwarding Tom’s reply. Quick asks for internal owners so we can bundle and send to Sara by EOD Friday:

- Karthik: can you produce a 2-slide technical summary (PoC scope, integration checklist, expected latency/cost uplift) and a short demo script (3 min) showing the Redis-backed KV cache + batching benefits? Reference the PoC scope attachment.
- Vivek: can you prepare an internal enablement one-pager focused on CS/ops handoff, success criteria, and support SLA expectations? Include a suggested escalation path.
- Marissa: can you draft the 1-page business case and two 30s executive soundbites aimed at the CFO (Kristen Park)? We need a concise ROI line (projected cost savings and time-to-value).

Also tagging Legal/Security — Amy asked about redlines; we should have a standard clause callout ready. I’ll compile our SOC2 evidence packet and the short controls summary.

Goal: send a packaged email to Sara with: 1) one-pager business case, 2) technical 2-slide summary (PDF), 3) internal enablement one-pager, 4) draft MSA + DPA (redline-ready), and 5) PoC scope. If we can get those pieces by Friday 5pm PT I’ll send them over and ask Sara to kick off Procurement.

Thanks — Alex

Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap + quick asks (next steps) — prep for internal sell-in

Nice — team, thanks for the quick turnaround. A few pragmatic items to include in the deliverable pack to increase traction with Finance/Legal/Procurement:

1) Business case (Marissa) — include an ASAP ROI calc: baseline cost per inference today, projected cost after Redwood optimizations, and 12-month run-rate savings. Provide a conservative and upside case (mid & high confidence). Keep it to one page with a single table and 3 bullet callouts.

2) Exec soundbites — two options:
   a) CFO-friendly (risk + savings): "Redwood will deliver measurable savings on inference spend while maintaining accuracy — expect a 12-month payback on pilot scale and strong downside protection via auto-fallbacks."
   b) Product/ops (time-to-value): "We’ll validate in 6 weeks and be able to scale to full production without re-architecting the scoring pipeline — minimal engineering lift, predictable latency."

3) Procurement/legal checklist — short table indicating typical turnaround times and which clauses to expect redlines on (data residency, indemnity caps, SOC2 clause). Karthik/Vivek — flag anything that adds >2 weeks to the schedule.

4) Technical appendix (Karthik) — include expected p95 numbers based on our internal benchmarks for similar customers and an integration checklist (API keys, network allowlist, test dataset format).

I’ll review drafts on Monday morning; if we hit the EOD Friday send target we should be able to land the Procurement kick by the week of Sep 20 and target Finance approval week of Oct 4 as requested.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189
